idea_name: Equalizer of hypothesis vs empirical ATR→range morphisms
mechanism: Band %ΔATR (10×~20% bands from −100..+100) into domain A and %Δ(high−low) into B. Morphism f=hypothesis isomorphism (same band→same band); morphism g=argmax empirical count from a lagged cross-table on training bars. Equalizer E⊂A is the subset of ATR bands where f and g land on the same range band. Live: only if new %ΔATR∈E (universal-property inclusion) emit the agreed range-change forecast for trailing; else abstain.
data_needed: ATR series and bar high−low; training window for cross-table; band grid; lag (1 bar in article)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD.ln M5; train 2021-01-01→2022-01-01; EURGBP mentioned in methods
why_new_for_mis: Builds a disagreement filter: volatility forecasts fire only on ATR states where theory and history agree—an explicit abstain/trust gate MIS can reuse for any indicator→vol map.
quote: based on these two morphisms we can determine within the domain (percentage changes in ATR) which percentage bands are matched by both morphisms to the same percentage bands in the codomain

idea_name: Multi-domain nearest-neighbor commute for bar-range change
mechanism: Source multi-domain of lagged multi-dim features (Δhigh/Δlow at 1–2 lags; optional more lags) maps by homomorphism to codomain of normalized % change in price-bar range ∈{−100..100 step 20}. Inference: winner-takes-all nearest Euclidean neighbor in the multi-domain, then read its morphism’s codomain. Square commute yields two projection paths; combine by min, mean, or max of the two % forecasts and scale ATR/stop by that factor.
data_needed: OHLC lags; trained homomorphism tables; commute aggregator choice (min/mean/max)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURGBP D1 2022.01.01–2022.08.01; Awesome Oscillator signal; trailing vs MA-trail control
why_new_for_mis: Turns lagged multi-feature bags (with repetitions) into a discrete bar-range volatility sensor with dual-path commute consensus—usable as a trail-width or vol-regime input.
quote: we will take a deeper look at the various types of special/unique domains one can come across and also explore how their relationships can be used to moderate expectations in price volatility

idea_name: Indexed MA-ribbon morphism weights as trend-continuation sensor
mechanism: Index domain N = MA periods; E/E′ = MAs on typical vs median (or close/WAP) price. Morphisms f between same-period MAs across applied-prices (or across periods 21↔34) carry weights; tracking weight changes along the ribbon quantifies how much trend remains vs imminent reversal.
data_needed: Multiple MA buffers by period and applied price; time series of morphism weights
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic MA ribbon illustration; same EURGBP D1 trailing context elsewhere in article
why_new_for_mis: Reframes MA ribbon as an indexed-domain morphism-weight stream for continuation/reversal sensing rather than only crossover signals.
quote: if we track the changes to the weights in these morphisms we could quantify how much a trend has left to continue or whether a reversal is happening soon

idea_name: Monoid tournament over lookback/TF/price/indicator then trend-vs-range
mechanism: Five monoids with identity + associative binary ops ∈{LEAST,MOST,CLOSEST,FURTHEST}: (1) lookback∈{1..8}×4 bars weighted by ABS(A)/(ABS(A)+ABS(B)) relative move; (2) TF∈{H1..D1} same %close-change weight; (3) applied price∈{median,typical,open,close} weighted by stdev over chosen lookback; (4) RSI vs Bollinger normalized to 0–100 via (C/(|C|+|D|)+1)×50; (5) trade-with-trend vs trade-with-range weighted by pullback-points / period-range (range weight ∈[0,1], trend=1−that). Operate_8→4→2 tournament picks one setting per monoid for trailing.
data_needed: Close/high/low; RSI; Bollinger mid/upper/lower; optimizable op+identity per monoid
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: H1 testing TF; analysis TFs H1–D1; RSI signal + fixed-money EA trailing tests
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a discrete regime bit (trend vs range) co-selected with lookback/TF/vol features via the same monoid reduction—not a separate heuristic.
quote: To quantify these two elements we’ll consider, over the selected lookback period, the amount of price points a security pulls back counter to its eventual trend at the end of the period, as a percentage of this periods total price range

idea_name: Stdev-weighted applied-price monoid as local volatility selector
mechanism: Applied-price monoid elements {MODE_MEDIAN, MODE_TYPICAL, MODE_OPEN, MODE_CLOSE} are scored by the standard deviation of that series over the monoid-chosen lookback; binary monoid ops then pick the applied price used downstream for indicator/trailing logic.
data_needed: OHLC→applied-price series; lookback length; monoid op/identity
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same H1 trailing CT setup; TF monoid H1–D1
why_new_for_mis: Selects which price definition is currently most volatile as an explicit sensing step—MIS can treat chosen applied-price identity as a microstructure/vol-channel state.
quote: In this case we’ll use the standard deviation of each applied price over the period selected in look back period to determine the weighting or value of each applied price

idea_name: Calendar product universal-property pair-value when one currency lags
mechanism: Schema tables (events, types, currencies, currency-pair values) as a category-theory product/square commute. Homomorphisms map events→types and events→currencies; reverse legs from pair-values; universal-property homomorphism da maps a weighted pair composite (e.g. EURUSD PMI) back to constituent calendar rows. When only one currency’s print is fresh, commuting forecasts the missing side’s contribution into a timestamped pair-level value for correlation to subsequent price and for sizing.
data_needed: MqlCalendarEvent/Value streams; event-type taxonomy; bid/ask currency weights; pair list
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: PMI focus; EUR,GBP,USD,CHF,JPY; pairs EURUSD,GBPUSD,USDCHF,USDJPY; H1 chart context in logs
why_new_for_mis: Turns asynchronous dual-currency calendar releases into a single lagged pair-macro sensor with an explicit fill-in for the stale leg—MIS can stream pair-event values beside price.
quote: with category theory we can actually use the universal property to anticipate or forecast the value for the currency that is not updated since the diagram commutes

idea_name: Exogenous linear-order functor (ocean tides)→index range volatility
mechanism: Domain category: daily Monterey NOAA tide heights as linear-order objects (3–4 heights/day) with consecutive-day morphisms. Codomain: NASDAQ (high−low)/point over matching windows. Functor either maps objects→objects or morphisms→morphisms (Δtide→Δrange) with a 1-day lag; linear coefficients via regression helper M(); output scales trailing stop. Object-map vs morphism-map tested separately.
data_needed: Normalized tide CSV (datetime+heights); NASDAQ OHLC; lag=1D; functor mode flag
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: NASDAQ; D1; 2020-01-01→2020-03-15 (COVID window); Awesome Oscillator + fixed margin
why_new_for_mis: Concrete exogenous→equity volatility lag sensor (non-price domain) with dual functor checks—pattern MIS can reuse for any alt-data linear order→range map.
quote: we will step outside of the box, and for this article look at bridging ocean-tide data gathered off California’s coast to the volatility of the NASDAQ Index

idea_name: Economic-calendar graph functor to equity bar-range volatility
mechanism: Build graph category with cycle vertices retail-sales→CPI→10y auction→PMI (edges=hypothesis dependence); each object holds latest four prints. Codomain: index (high−low)/point on MN1 as volatility (not VIX). Functor object-map and morphism-map (Δecon→Δvol) with linear coeffs; optional NormalizeForecast for negative projections. Same coeffs transfer-tested USD→SPX, EUR/DE→DAX, GBP→FTSE.
data_needed: Calendar values by type/country/currency; index MqlRates; morph constant; optional normalizer
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: SPX500 MN1 2020–2023; GER30; UK100; USD/EUR/GBP calendar subsets
why_new_for_mis: Macro graph→realized-range volatility sensor with cross-market coefficient transfer—MIS can host a calendar-graph channel feeding equity vol regimes.
quote: the purpose of this article therefore, will like our previous one, seek to demonstrate the volatility forecasting potential of functors between two categories

idea_name: MLP-as-functor from calendar graph to SPX monthly trend delta
mechanism: Same four-node economic graph as domain; codomain is linear-order of S&P 500 index changes (trend, not only vol). Two AlgLib MLPs (inputs=4, hidden≈5–12, output=1) act as object-functor vs morphism-functor; Levenberg–Marquardt train on CSV calendar→ΔSPX; MLPProcess yields forecast used in Expert Signal Long/ShortCondition. Weights persisted across optimization if equity improves.
data_needed: CSV calendar features + target ΔSPX; train/test date split; hidden size; decay/restarts
why_new_for_mis: Elevates functors from linear maps to sequence-capable MLP sensors for directional index change—direct neural_sensor pattern for MIS macro→trend channels.
quote: This implementation will be achieved with the help of a multi-layer perceptron… projected change in the S&P 500

idea_name: Naturality-square MLP commute for multi-horizon range forecasts
mechanism: Codomain naturality square corners A/B/C/D log distinct bar-range changes: ATR-path 1-bar vs 2-bar ahead and BB-path 2-bar-span ranges at +1/+2 functor horizons (normalized Δrange/(range_t+range_{t+k})). Horizontal edges=natural transformations (MLP transformers); vertical edges=functor-image MLPs. Train four small MLPs per bar (optional m_extra_training); any two commuting legs cross-check a farther-horizon range forecast for trailing. Domain ATR/BB % changes (21 bins −100..100) motivate the functors but square alone drives the forecast.
data_needed: High/low series; optional ATR/BB %Δ bins; four MLP weight sets; extra_training length
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD D1 2022.08.01–2023.08.01; prior-year forward check negative
why_new_for_mis: Multi-horizon volatility sensor with built-in commute consistency across four range definitions—MIS can treat path disagreement as a confidence/regime flag.
quote: This allows us to check our forecasts since any two legs could produce a projection. The four corners of the square reflect different forecasts at some point in the future of changes in the range of our price bars

mechanism: Phase-space reconstruction (lag, embed dim) + nearest-neighbor divergence log-ratio yields a local Lyapunov exponent on close; positive⇒chaotic, negative⇒stable. Script also tallies trend reversals/continuations vs sign(Lyapunov) on EURUSD H1. Not mined for MIS: Lyapunov/chaos-physics sensing lane is closed per reader contract.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 statistical script; InpDataLength=1000 default indicator window
